name: libloans
requirements: T1 Money amounts. Librarians enter and read amounts of money the same way everywhere. Package `money` provides `type Cents int64`, `var ErrInvalidAmount error`, `func Parse(s string) (Cents, error)` and `func (c Cents) String() string`. Parse accepts a non-negative amount written as 1 to 9 ASCII digits, optionally followed by a dot and exactly two digits. Examples: "0" -> 0, "7" -> 700, "12.50" -> 1250, "007.05" -> 705. Parse rejects everything else: the empty string, leading or trailing whitespace, a sign, a currency symbol, commas, one or three decimal digits, a trailing dot, and more than 9 integer digits. On rejection it returns 0 and an error for which errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidAmount) is true. String renders a dollar sign, then the whole-dollar part with no leading zeros and no thousands separators, then a dot and exactly two cent digits. Examples: 1250 -> "$12.50", 5 -> "$0.05", 0 -> "$0.00", 123456 -> "$1234.56". Negative amounts get a minus sign before the dollar sign: -305 -> "-$3.05".

T2 ISBNs. Staff can type an ISBN in any common form, and the system always stores the same 13-digit form. Package `isbn` provides `type ISBN string`, `var ErrInvalidISBN error`, `func Parse(s string) (ISBN, error)` and `func (i ISBN) String() string`. Parse first trims leading and trailing whitespace, then removes every hyphen and space anywhere in the input. The remaining text must be one of two things. (a) 13 ASCII digits with a valid ISBN-13 checksum: weight the digits 1,3,1,3,... from the left, and the weighted sum must be divisible by 10. (b) A valid ISBN-10: nine digits followed by a digit or an 'X'/'x' (meaning 10), where the sum of each character's value times (10 minus its zero-based position) is divisible by 11. An ISBN-10 is converted by putting "978" in front of its first nine digits and appending a new ISBN-13 check digit, computed as (10 - (weighted sum of the first 12 digits mod 10)) mod 10. The result is always exactly 13 digits. Examples: "0-306-40615-2" -> "9780306406157", "978 0 306 40615 7" -> "9780306406157", "080442957X" is accepted. Any other input, including a bad check digit or an 'X' in a non-final position, returns "" and an error matching ErrInvalidISBN. String returns the 13 digits unchanged.

T3 Calendar dates. Loans are tracked by calendar day, with no time of day and no time zone. Package `calendar` provides `type Date` (a struct whose fields are left to the implementer), `var ErrInvalidDate error`, `func New(year int, month time.Month, day int) (Date, error)`, `func Parse(s string) (Date, error)`, `func (d Date) String() string`, `func (d Date) AddDays(n int) Date`, `func (d Date) Weekday() time.Weekday` and `func DaysBetween(from, to Date) int`. New and Parse accept only years 1000 through 9999 and only days that exist in the Gregorian calendar: 2028-02-29 is valid, 2027-02-29 and 2026-04-31 are not. Parse accepts exactly the form YYYY-MM-DD with a two-digit month and day, for example "2026-11-10". It rejects "2026-1-5", "2026/11/10", surrounding whitespace and anything with a time part. Both return the zero Date and an error matching ErrInvalidDate on failure. String returns YYYY-MM-DD. AddDays moves forward by n calendar days, or back when n is negative, crossing month and year ends: 2026-12-30 plus 3 is 2027-01-02. Behaviour outside years 1000-9999 is not specified. DaysBetween returns the signed number of whole days from `from` to `to`: (2026-11-01, 2026-11-10) -> 9, the reverse -> -9, the same day -> 0. Weekday returns the day of the week; 2026-11-10 is a Tuesday. Two Dates for the same day are equal under ==.

T4 Item kinds and due dates. When an item is checked out, the patron is told when it is due. Package `lending` provides `type ItemKind int` with constants `Book`, `DVD` and `Magazine` (the zero value is not a valid kind), `var ErrUnknownKind error`, `func ParseKind(s string) (ItemKind, error)`, `func (k ItemKind) String() string` and `func DueDate(kind ItemKind, from calendar.Date) (calendar.Date, error)`. Loan periods are 21 days for a book, 7 days for a DVD and 14 days for a magazine. The due date is `from` plus the loan period. The library is closed on Sundays, so a due date that falls on a Sunday moves to the following Monday. Examples: a book from 2026-11-10 is due 2026-12-01; a DVD from 2026-11-08 lands on Sunday 2026-11-15 and is due 2026-11-16. ParseKind trims surrounding whitespace and accepts "book", "dvd" or "magazine" in any letter case. Anything else returns 0 and an error matching ErrUnknownKind. String returns "book", "dvd" or "magazine", and "unknown" for any other value. DueDate with an invalid kind returns the zero Date and an error matching ErrUnknownKind.

T5 Late fines. A patron who returns an item late pays a daily fine, up to a cap per item. Package `lending` provides `func Fine(kind ItemKind, due, returned calendar.Date) (money.Cents, error)`. Days late is the number of calendar days from `due` to `returned`. Sundays count, and there is no grace period. If days late is 0 or less, the fine is $0.00, so returning on the due date is free. Otherwise the fine is the smaller of (days late x daily rate) and the cap. Rates and caps: book $0.25 per day, capped at $10.00; DVD $1.00 per day, capped at $15.00; magazine $0.10 per day, capped at $3.00. Examples: a book due 2026-11-02 and returned 2026-11-06 -> $1.00 (100 cents); a DVD returned 20 days late -> $15.00; a magazine returned early -> $0.00. An invalid kind returns 0 and an error matching ErrUnknownKind.

T6 Renewals. A patron can extend a loan, within limits. Package `lending` provides `func Renew(l Loan, today calendar.Date, renewalsSoFar int, holdPending bool) (calendar.Date, error)` and the errors `ErrAlreadyReturned`, `ErrNotRenewable`, `ErrOnHold`, `ErrRenewalLimit` and `ErrOverdue`. The checks run in this order, and the first one that fails decides the error: (1) l.Returned is not nil -> ErrAlreadyReturned; (2) l.Kind is not a valid kind -> ErrUnknownKind; (3) l.Kind is Magazine -> ErrNotRenewable; (4) holdPending is true -> ErrOnHold; (5) renewalsSoFar is 2 or more -> ErrRenewalLimit; (6) today is after l.Due -> ErrOverdue. Renewing on the due date itself is allowed. Every failure returns the zero Date with an error for which errors.Is matches the named error. On success the new due date is today plus the kind's loan period (book 21 days, DVD 7 days), moved to Monday if it falls on a Sunday. If that date is not later than l.Due, l.Due is returned unchanged. Example: a book due 2026-12-01, renewed on 2026-11-28 with no hold and 0 prior renewals -> 2026-12-19.

T7 Loan records. The circulation desk exports one loan per line, and the system reads those lines. Package `lending` provides `type Loan struct { Patron string; ISBN isbn.ISBN; Title string; Kind ItemKind; Borrowed calendar.Date; Due calendar.Date; Returned *calendar.Date }`, `var ErrMalformedLine error` and `func ParseLoan(line string) (Loan, error)`. A line has exactly six fields separated by '|', in this order: patron, ISBN, title, kind, borrowed date, returned date. Each field is trimmed of surrounding whitespace. Patron and title must not be empty. The ISBN may be in any form T2 accepts and is stored as 13 digits. The kind may be in any form T4's ParseKind accepts. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. An empty returned field means the item is still on loan, and Returned is nil. Otherwise the returned date must not be earlier than the borrowed date. Due is the standard due date for the kind, counted from the borrowed date: the kind's loan period, moved to Monday if it falls on a Sunday. Errors (all return the zero Loan): the wrong number of fields, an empty patron or title, or a returned date before the borrowed date -> ErrMalformedLine; a bad ISBN -> isbn.ErrInvalidISBN; a bad kind -> ErrUnknownKind; a bad date -> calendar.ErrInvalidDate. Callers check each with errors.Is. Example: "Ada Lovelace | 0-306-40615-2 | Notes on the Engine | Book | 2026-11-10 |" -> Patron "Ada Lovelace", ISBN "9780306406157", Title "Notes on the Engine", Kind Book, Borrowed 2026-11-10, Due 2026-12-01, Returned nil.

T8 Overdue report. Each morning staff print a list of everything overdue. Package `report` provides `func Overdue(loans []lending.Loan, asOf calendar.Date) string`. A loan is listed when all of these hold: its Kind is book, DVD or magazine; Borrowed is on or before asOf; it is not returned as of asOf (Returned is nil or after asOf); and Due, taken from the Loan as given, is strictly before asOf. Days late is the number of calendar days from Due to asOf. The accrued fine is the smaller of (days late x daily rate) and the cap: book $0.25 per day capped at $10.00, DVD $1.00 per day capped at $15.00, magazine $0.10 per day capped at $3.00. Rows are sorted by days late (descending), then patron, then ISBN, then title (each ascending, byte order). Output: the first line is "OVERDUE AS OF <asOf YYYY-MM-DD>". Then comes one row per loan, made of these fields separated by a single tab: patron, 13-digit ISBN, title, "due <Due YYYY-MM-DD>", "<n> day late" when n is 1 or "<n> days late" otherwise, and the fine formatted like "$2.00". The last line is "TOTAL <count> item <sum>" when count is 1, otherwise "TOTAL <count> items <sum>", where sum is the total of the listed fines in the same money format. Every line, including the last, ends with "
". With nothing overdue the output is the header followed by "TOTAL 0 items $0.00
". Example, with asOf 2026-11-10 and 	 standing for a tab: "OVERDUE AS OF 2026-11-10
Ada Lovelace	9780306406157	Notes on the Engine	due 2026-11-02	8 days late	$2.00
Bob Byte	9780000000002	Space Film	due 2026-11-09	1 day late	$1.00
TOTAL 2 items $3.00
". In this example Ada's loan is a book and Bob's is a DVD.

T9 Patron statement. At the desk, staff can print one patron's account. Package `report` provides `var ErrUnknownPatron error` and `func Statement(loans []lending.Loan, patron string, asOf calendar.Date) (string, error)`. Only loans meet all of these count: Patron equals `patron` exactly (case-sensitive, no trimming), Kind is book, DVD or magazine, and Borrowed is on or before asOf. If no loan counts, Statement returns "" and an error matching ErrUnknownPatron. A counted loan is on loan if Returned is nil or after asOf. Otherwise it is returned, and it appears only if it was returned late (Returned after Due). Fines use these rates and caps: book $0.25 per day capped at $10.00, DVD $1.00 per day capped at $15.00, magazine $0.10 per day capped at $3.00. A returned-late loan is charged for the days from Due to Returned. An on-loan loan with Due strictly before asOf is charged for the days from Due to asOf. Output lines, each ending in "
": "STATEMENT FOR <patron> AS OF <asOf>"; then "ON LOAN"; then one line per on-loan item, sorted by Due, then title, then ISBN (ascending): two spaces, then "<title> (<isbn>) due <Due>", plus " OVERDUE <fine>" when Due is before asOf; then "RETURNED LATE"; then one line per returned-late item, sorted by Returned, then title, then ISBN: two spaces, then "<title> (<isbn>) returned <Returned> fine <fine>"; and finally "BALANCE <sum of all fines shown>". An empty section shows the single line "  none". Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, ISBNs are 13 digits, and money is formatted like "$2.00". Example: "STATEMENT FOR Ada Lovelace AS OF 2026-11-10
ON LOAN
  Notes on the Engine (9780306406157) due 2026-11-02 OVERDUE $2.00
RETURNED LATE
  none
BALANCE $2.00
".

allocation.A: Developer A owns T3, T1, T5 and T8: finish T3 (calendar) first and hand it to B, because B's due dates and record parsing depend on it; then T1 (money), then T5 (fines), which goes to B for T9; and finally T8 (overdue report), tested end to end once B hands off T7.
allocation.B: Developer B owns T2, T4, T7, T6 and T9: start with T2 (ISBN), then do T4 (item kinds and due dates) as soon as T3 arrives and hand it to A for T5; then T7 (loan records), which goes to A for T8; then T6 (renewals); and finally T9 (patron statement) once A has handed off T5.

milestones.trigger: host-only: the first accepted share whose diff adds a call to the release_on_call function in a non-test .go file outside its package, else the first agent's ready (#509)
requirements: Correction to T3: `DaysBetween` must count both the start and the end day, not only the days after the start. 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-10 is 10, not 9. A date to itself is 1, not 0. When `to` is earlier, the result is the negative of the count from `to` to `from`, so 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-01 is -10, not -9.
